label: phospholipid
definition_first_300_chars: A lipid containing phosphoric acid as a mono- or di-ester. The term encompasses phosphatidic acids and phosphoglycerides.

label: NADPH
definition_first_300_chars: The reduced form of NADP+; used in anabolic reactions, such as lipid and nucleic acid synthesis, which require NADPH as a reducing agent.

label: glucose
definition_first_300_chars: An aldohexose used as a source of energy and metabolic intermediate.

label: thymine
definition_first_300_chars: A pyrimidine nucleobase that is uracil in which the hydrogen at position 5 is replaced by a methyl group.

label: transfer RNA
definition_first_300_chars: A single-stranded RNA molecule containing about 70-90 nucleotides, folded by intrastrand base pairing into a characteristic secondary ('cloverleaf') structure that carries a specific amino acid and matches it to its corresponding codon on an mRNA during protein synthesis.

label: nucleobase
definition_first_300_chars: That part of DNA or RNA that may be involved in pairing.

label: polymer
definition_first_300_chars: A polymer is a mixture, which is composed of macromolecules of different kinds and which may be differentiated by composition, length, degree of branching etc..

label: poison
definition_first_300_chars: Any substance that causes disturbance to organisms by chemical reaction or other activity on the molecular scale, when a sufficient quantity is absorbed by the organism.

label: type B pancreatic cell
definition_first_300_chars: Pancreatic beta cells are also reportedly CD284-positive. Upon activation, they upregulate their CD14 expression.

label: leukocyte
definition_first_300_chars: An achromatic cell of the myeloid or lymphoid lineages capable of ameboid movement, found in blood or other tissue.

label: chromatin
definition_first_300_chars: Chromosomes include parts that are not part of the chromatin. Examples include the kinetochore.

label: nucleus
definition_first_300_chars: A membrane-bounded organelle of eukaryotic cells in which chromosomes are housed and replicated. definition_first_300_chars: Chromosomes include parts that are not part of the chromatin. Examples include the kinetochore.

label: lysosome
definition_first_300_chars: A small lytic vacuole that has cell cycle-independent morphology found in most animal cells and that contains a variety of hydrolases, most of which have their maximal activities in the pH range 5-6. label: cytoskeleton
definition_first_300_chars: A cellular structure that forms the internal framework of eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells. label: plasma membrane
definition_first_300_chars: The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.

label: glucose catabolic process
definition_first_300_chars: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of glucose, the aldohexose gluco-hexose.

label: oxidative phosphorylation
definition_first_300_chars: The phosphorylation of ADP to ATP that accompanies the oxidation of a metabolite through the operation of the respiratory chain. Oxidation of compounds establishes a proton gradient across the membrane, providing the energy for ATP synthesis.

label: endocytosis
definition_first_300_chars: A cellular process in which cells take up external materials or membrane constituents by the invagination of a part of the plasma membrane to form a new membrane-bounded vesicle.

label: digestion
definition_first_300_chars: The whole of the physical, chemical, and biochemical processes carried out by multicellular organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

label: blood circulation
definition_first_300_chars: The flow of blood through the body of an animal, enabling the transport of nutrients to the tissues and the removal of waste products.

label: cell death
definition_first_300_chars: This term should not be used for direct annotation, it is currently kept in GO as a placeholder for describing cell death phenotypes in uPHENO. label: biosynthetic process
definition_first_300_chars: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism synthesizes chemical substances. This typically represents the energy-requiring part of metabolism in which simpler substances are transformed into more complex ones.

label: endomembrane system
definition_first_300_chars: A collection of membranous structures involved in transport within the cell. The main components of the endomembrane system are endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi bodies, vesicles, cell membrane and nuclear envelope. label: protein transport
definition_first_300_chars: The directed movement of proteins into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: ligand-gated monoatomic ion channel activity
definition_first_300_chars: Enables the transmembrane transfer of an ion by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

label: energy coupled proton transport, down electrochemical gradient
definition_first_300_chars: The transport of protons across a membrane to generate an electrochemical gradient (proton-motive force) that provides energy for the synthesis of ATP or GTP.

label: passive transmembrane transporter activity
definition_first_300_chars: Enables the transfer of a single solute from one side of a membrane to the other by a mechanism involving conformational change, either by facilitated diffusion or in a membrane potential dependent process if the solute is charged.

label: active transmembrane transporter activity
definition_first_300_chars: Enables the transfer of a specific substance or related group of substances from one side of a membrane to the other, up the solute's concentration gradient. The transporter binds the solute and undergoes a series of conformational changes. Transport works equally well in either direction.

label: respiratory electron transport chain
definition_first_300_chars: A process in which a series of electron carriers operate together to transfer electrons from donors such as NADH and FADH2 to any of several different terminal electron acceptors to generate a transmembrane electrochemical gradient.

label: myofibril
definition_first_300_chars: The contractile element of skeletal and cardiac muscle; a long, highly organized bundle of actin, myosin, and other proteins that contracts by a sliding filament mechanism.

label: erythrocyte differentiation
definition_first_300_chars: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires specializes features of an erythrocyte.

label: motile cilium
definition_first_300_chars: A cilium which may have a variable arrangement of axonemal microtubules and also contains molecular motors. It may beat with a whip-like pattern that promotes cell motility or transport of fluids and other cells across a cell surface, such as on epithelial cells that line the lumenal ducts of variou

label: monoatomic ion channel complex
definition_first_300_chars: A protein complex that spans a membrane and forms a water-filled channel across the phospholipid bilayer allowing selective monoatomic ion transport down its electrochemical gradient.

label: myofilament
definition_first_300_chars: Any of the smallest contractile units of a myofibril (striated muscle fiber).

label: sarcolemma
definition_first_300_chars: The outer membrane of a muscle cell, consisting of the plasma membrane, a covering basement membrane (about 100 nm thick and sometimes common to more than one fiber), and the associated loose network of collagen fibers.

label: proton-transporting ATP synthase complex
definition_first_300_chars: A proton-transporting two-sector ATPase complex that catalyzes the phosphorylation of ADP to ATP during oxidative phosphorylation. label: monoatomic ion homeostasis
definition_first_300_chars: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of monoatomic ions within an organism or cell. Monatomic ions (also called simple ions) are ions consisting of exactly one atom.

label: cell division
definition_first_300_chars: Note that this term differs from 'cytokinesis ; GO:0000910' in that cytokinesis does not include nuclear division.

label: meiotic cell cycle
definition_first_300_chars: Note that this term should not be confused with 'GO:0140013 ; meiotic nuclear division'. 'GO:0051321 ; meiotic cell cycle represents the entire mitotic cell cycle, while 'GO:0140013 meiotic nuclear division' specifically represents the actual nuclear division step of the mitotic cell cycle.

label: membrane depolarization
definition_first_300_chars: The process in which membrane potential decreases with respect to its steady-state potential, usually from negative potential to a more positive potential. label: transmembrane transport
definition_first_300_chars: Transmembrane transport is the transport of a solute across a lipid bilayer. Note that transport through the nuclear pore complex is not transmembrane because the nuclear membrane is a double membrane and is not traversed. For transport through the nuclear pore, consider instead the term 'nucleocyto

label: motor behavior
definition_first_300_chars: The specific neuromuscular movement of a single organism in response to external or internal stimuli.

label: mitotic spindle
definition_first_300_chars: A spindle that forms as part of mitosis. Mitotic and meiotic spindles contain distinctive complements of proteins associated with microtubules.

label: membrane protein complex
definition_first_300_chars: Any protein complex that is part of a membrane.

label: leaf
definition_first_300_chars: A phyllome (PO:0006001) that is not associated with a reproductive structure.

label: erythropoietin
definition_first_300_chars: Category=gene.

label: preproinsulin
definition_first_300_chars: Category=gene.

label: primer
definition_first_300_chars: An oligo to which new deoxyribonucleotides can be added by DNA polymerase.

label: ganglion
definition_first_300_chars: A biological tissue mass, most commonly a mass of nerve cell bodies.

label: organ
definition_first_300_chars: Anatomical structure that performs a specific function or group of functions [WP].

label: blood
definition_first_300_chars: A fluid that is composed of blood plasma and erythrocytes.

label: limbic system
definition_first_300_chars: includes the hippocampus, amygdala, anterior thalamic nuclei, and limbic cortex, which support a variety of functions including emotion, behavior, long term memory, and olfaction [Wikipedia]

label: aorta
definition_first_300_chars: The main trunk of the systemic arterial system that carries blood from the heart to all the organs and other structures of the body, bringing oxygenated blood to all parts of the body in the systemic circulation.

label: brain
definition_first_300_chars: The brain is the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate, and most invertebrate, animals. Some primitive animals such as jellyfish and starfish have a decentralized nervous system without a brain, while sponges lack any nervous system at all. In vertebrates, the brain is located in the head,

label: digestive system
definition_first_300_chars: Anatomical system that has as its parts the organs devoted to the ingestion, digestion, and assimilation of food and the discharge of residual wastes.

label: circulatory system
definition_first_300_chars: Organ system that passes nutrients (such as amino acids and electrolytes), gases, hormones, blood cells, etc. to and from cells in the body to help fight diseases and help stabilize body temperature and pH to maintain homeostasis[WP].

label: saliva-secreting gland
definition_first_300_chars: Saliva-secreting exocrine glands of the oral cavity[GO].

label: skeletal muscle tissue
definition_first_300_chars: Muscle tissue that consists primarily of skeletal muscle fibers.

label: muscle organ
definition_first_300_chars: Organ consisting of a tissue made up of various elongated cells that are specialized to contract and thus to produce movement and mechanical work[GO].

label: artery
definition_first_300_chars: An epithelial tube or tree of tibes that transports blood away from the heart[modified from AEO definition].

label: amygdala
definition_first_300_chars: Subcortical brain region lying anterior to the hippocampal formation in the temporal lobe and anterior to the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle in some species. It is usually subdivided into several groups. Functionally, it is not considered a unitary structure (MM).

label: dorsal plus ventral thalamus
definition_first_300_chars: Subcortical brain region consisting of paired gray matter bodies in the dorsal diencephalon and forming part of the lateral wall of the third ventricle of the brain. The thalamus represents the major portion of the diencephalon and is commonly divided into cellular aggregates known as nuclear groups

label: venule
definition_first_300_chars: One of the minute vessels that collect deoxygenated blood from the capillary plexuses returns it to the veins.

label: blood vessel
definition_first_300_chars: A vessel through which blood circulates in the body.

label: gray matter
definition_first_300_chars: A nervous system structure composed primarily of nerve cell bodies (somas). May also include dendrites and the initial unmyelinated portion of axons.

label: lung
definition_first_300_chars: Snakes and limbless lizards typically possess only the right lung as a major respiratory organ; the left lung is greatly reduced, or even absent. Amphisbaenians, however, have the opposite arrangement, with a major left lung, and a reduced or absent right lung [WP]

label: appendicular skeleton
definition_first_300_chars: Subdivision of skeleton which which consists of all the skeletal elements in in the pectoral and pelvic appendage complexes[cjm].

label: skin of body
definition_first_300_chars: The organ covering the body that consists of the dermis and epidermis.

label: gallbladder
definition_first_300_chars: Rats do not have a gallbladder, but produce bile. The bile flows directly from the liver through the (hepatic) bile duct into the small intestine (Hebel and Stromberg, 1988)

label: alveolus of lung
definition_first_300_chars: Spherical outcropping of the respiratory bronchioles and primary site of gas exchange with the blood. Alveoli are particular to mammalian lungs. Different structures are involved in gas exchange in other vertebrates[WP].

label: bone marrow
definition_first_300_chars: The soft tissue that fills the cavities of bones.

label: forelimb zeugopod
definition_first_300_chars: The middle limb segment of the pectoral free limb, between the autopod and stylopod segments. Includes as parts the forelimb zeugopodial skeleton, which includes as parts the radius and ulna, or their cartilage precursors, or evolutionary variants.

label: scapula
definition_first_300_chars: Endochondral bone that is dorsoventrally compressed and provides attachment site for muscles of the pectoral appendage.

label: digestive system element
definition_first_300_chars: Any of the organs or elements that are part of the digestive system. Examples: tongue, esophagus, spleen, crop, lunge feeding organ, tooth elements.
